close_reason: All four RFC 8620 §5.4 mandates now implemented in handle_contact_card_copy mirroring canonical mail-server: (1) same-account rejection with invalidArguments, (2) ifFromInState source-state precondition, (3) onSuccessDestroyOriginal with synthetic ContactCard/set invocation per RFC 8620 §6.3, (4) destroyFromIfInState gating the implicit destroy. 8 new unit tests + 1 end-to-end integration test against MemoryBackend verify the full cascade. Implementation in commit 4f64602.
description:
Trigger: any ContactCard/copy call. RFC 8620 §5.4 (the base /copy contract that ContactCard/copy inherits per RFC 9610 §3.6) requires four behaviors that handle_contact_card_copy does NOT implement:

 1. accountId MUST be different to fromAccountId. Currently a request with the same value in both is happily processed: card is fetched from acc, copy_contact_card is invoked into acc, and a duplicate id appears in the same account. Compare crate-jmap-mail-server/src/email.rs:2263-2268 which DOES reject this with invalidArguments.

 2. ifFromInState — RFC 8620 §5.4 specifies a state string for the SOURCE account; if supplied, must match the source account's get_state, otherwise stateMismatch. Currently ignored. Only ifInState (destination) is checked.

 3. onSuccessDestroyOriginal: Boolean (default false) — RFC 8620 §5.4 mandates that on success, the server MUST issue an implicit Foo/set destroy against the source account for each successfully copied id, with its response appended as a separate Invocation. Currently the argument is silently dropped and no follow-up invocation is emitted. handle_contact_card_copy always returns vec![] for the extra invocations.

 4. destroyFromIfInState — the ifInState passed to the implicit destroy. Same fate as #3.

For a sibling check: crate-jmap-mail-server/src/email.rs:2244+ implements all four. Contacts diverges from the canonical extension-server template here.

Severity: P0. #1 is a data-integrity bug (silent duplicate-id creation in one account). #3/#4 are silent-data-loss vs silent-data-retention mismatches (the client asks the server to destroy originals; server cheerfully ignores). #2 is a lost-update race window.

The simplest minimal fix is to enforce #1 and reject the others as invalidArguments until properly implemented — but the cleanest fix is to mirror the canonical mail-server pattern.
title: ContactCard/copy missing RFC 8620 §5.4 mandates — accountId == fromAccountId, ifFromInState, onSuccessDestroyOriginal, destroyFromIfInState
